title: Managed Monitoring and Zscaler Managed Probes: where they run, what they chart and their subscription limits

prose.text: Managed Monitoring is the part of ZDX that runs probes from Zscaler's own cloud rather than from a user's device; the Managed view of the Probes page is in [[zdx.probes]]. {{managed-service}} {{managed-tiers}}

prose.label: Open.
prose.text: How Zscaler Managed Probes map to the contract's monitor types and its Zscaler Hosted Monitoring collections is not stated {{gap:managed-monitor-mapping}}.

managed-service.statement: Managed Monitoring operates from within the Zscaler cloud infrastructure as a multi-tenant service that groups Web and Cloud Path probes into independent collections; Zscaler Managed Probes, an extension to the probes for predefined and custom applications, monitor a specific service or application directly from a Zscaler data center to an endpoint destination.

quotes: Managed Monitoring operates from within the Zscaler cloud infrastructure as a multi-tenant service.
The service allows you to logically group Web and Cloud Path probes into independent collections to set up your own tests for monitoring performance.

As an extension to ZDX probes for predefined and custom applications, Zscaler Managed Probes monitor the performance of a specific service or application directly from a Zscaler data center to an endpoint destination.

managed-tiers.statement: In the subscription table Managed Monitoring is supported only as an add-on on Standard, Microsoft 365 and Advanced, with identical ranges and limitations across those add-ons, and on Advanced Plus allows 1 probe per 1,000 users for each managed location (columns in the order of the table's header row).

quotes: | Managed Monitoring* | Supported only as add-on | Supported only as add-on | Supported only as add-on | 1 probe per 1,000 users for each managed location |
- *Identical ranges and limitations across add-ons for Standard, Microsoft 365, and Advanced subscriptions.
| Feature | Standard | Microsoft 365 | Advanced | Advanced Plus |

managed-charts.statement: Managed Monitoring charts Availability and Page Fetch Time by default for Web probes and End-to-End Latency for Cloud Path probes; the first chart on the page defaults to the previous 30 days, and its time-range widget runs from 2 to 48 hours, defaulting to 24 hours.

quotes: Depending on the probe you've selected, charts are displayed by default for Availability and Page Fetch Time for Web probes, and End-to-End Latency for Cloud Path probes.
The default time range for the initial chart on the page is the previous 30 days.
The minimum time range for the widget is 2 hours, and the maximum time range is 48 hours. The default time range of the widget is 24 hours.

managed-availability.statement: Web probe availability is reported month to date (with the change from the previous month), over the past 30 days (with the change from the prior 30 days) and over the widget's time range (with the change from the prior 30 days); in the Page Fetch Time metrics section, each data point in a scatter chart is an individual probe run.

quotes: Month To Date (MTD): The average availability from the first day of the month to the current date, along with a percentage increase or decrease from the previous month.
Past 30 Days: The average availability within the past 30 days, along with a percentage increase or decrease from the prior 30 days.
Time range from widget: The average availability within your designated time range, along with a percentage increase or decrease from the prior 30 days.
Each data point within a scatter chart represents an individual probe run.

managed-run-details.statement: A Web probe run's details give, in milliseconds, redirect time, DNS, TCP, SSL handshake, server response time (TTFB) and page fetch time, with a response code (the HTTP informational or success code) per redirected URL; a Cloud Path probe run's details give end-to-end latency, packet loss, maximum hop count and jitter, and, separately, a Cloud Path visualization consolidates all managed locations into one image.

quotes: The following key metrics are provided in milliseconds on the Run Details page:
Redirect Time: The time measurement of traffic redirects.
DNS: The resolution time for the DNS name.
TCP: The time measurement of the Transmission Control Protocol.
SSL Handshake: The communication time to the device.
Page Fetch Time: The time it takes the application to load a page for the user.
Server Response Time: The Time to First Byte (TTFB).
Server redirect information is also provided per URL:
Response Code: The HTTP informational or success code.
End-to-End Latency: The time to send a data packet from source to destination, including hops between legs in the Cloud Path.
Packet Loss: When data packets that travel across a network fail to reach their destination.
Max Hop Count: The maximum number of Cloud Path hops before reaching the destination.
Jitter: The variance in time delay between data packets over a network.
This visualization consolidates all managed locations into one image.

managed-monitor-mapping.title: How Zscaler Managed Probes map to the contract's monitor types and Zscaler Hosted Monitoring collections
managed-monitor-mapping.detail: The help says Managed Monitoring groups Web and Cloud Path probes into collections and runs them from Zscaler data centers. The contract has collections for Zscaler Hosted Monitoring and End User Monitoring and four monitor types (WEB, TRACERT, TRACERT_V2, HIFI_MTR); no captured source says whether a Zscaler Managed Probe is a Zscaler Hosted Monitoring collection or which monitor types it uses. The articles on configuring and managing Zscaler Managed Probes (zdx-configuring-zscaler-managed-probes.json, zdx-managing-zscaler-managed-probes.json, zdx-zscaler-managed-probe-errors.json) were outside the extraction and are not read.
